newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sri Lankans seek bus ride from Australian wilderness.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankans seek bus ride from Australian wilderness.

text.p: A group of well-dressed Sri Lankan boatpeople were dropped on Australia's rugged and remote western coast and told to find a bus or train to the nearest civilisation, a search and rescue official said on Friday.

The 15 men spent three days wandering lost in dry, sandy bushland, far from any bus or train, until they were found by local fishermen and given food and water, emergency services worker Grant Shane said in a radio interview.
"They were clean and neat and well-dressed -- they actually made the fishermen look a bit sad," he said.
It is believed the group, aged between 18 and 42, are all related and were dropped off by a Taiwanese fishing boat after paying for their passage from their war-torn South Asian homeland.
"I gathered they've paid money, arrived on a boat, and (were told) -- 'Here it is, just wander inland a bit and you'll get picked up by a train or a bus'," the rescue official said.
The group was found near the west coast town of Exmouth, about 1,100 kilometres (680 miles) north of the Western Australian state capital Perth.
Immigration officials said the men had been taken to the Port Hedland refugee detention centre, further north, where they would be questioned. It was not yet known if they wanted asylum.

They were the second group of relatively well-off boatpeople to arrive in Australia in a month, fuelling fears this sparsely-populated affluent nation was being targetted by international migration racketeers.
A group of 139 well-dressed Chinese landed on the northern coastline in a modern, well-equipped boat last month.
